# graph query

`graph query` answers a read-only Cypher query in one call. Use it when a
question needs several hops, OR or NOT across relations, or counts and
grouping. For one type with field filters, one hop or a name, `find`,
`neighbors` and `lookup` stay the simple path.

- Labels are types (subtypes included), relationship types are relations,
  properties are fields and system fields such as `id` and `alias`. Write
  a type or relation by its local name (`(:<type>)`) when it is unique; its
  full CURIE always works when wrapped in backticks inside the query.
  `graph describe schema --json` lists every label, relationship pattern
  and property as the query writes them.
- Only active entities are nodes; `--include-inactive` adds superseded and
  retracted ones.
- Pass the query as one single-quoted argument. When quoting gets hard,
  write it to a file in the working directory and pass `--file <file>`.
  Bind values with `--param id=<id>` and use `$id` in the query. A value
  that parses as JSON is bound as JSON: `--param n=2.1` is the number 2.1,
  which never equals the text `"2.1"`. Quote such text (`--param 'n="2.1"'`)
  or write it into the query as a string.
- `--explain --json` shows how the query was understood (types, fields,
  parameters) and runs nothing. Use it when a result looks wrong.
- The query is read-only. Write with `apply` or the write commands.
- Rows are paged like `find`: follow `page.next_offset` or the hint.

| Part | Supported |
|---|---|
| Clauses | `MATCH`, `OPTIONAL MATCH`, `WHERE`, `WITH`, `UNWIND`, `RETURN`, `ORDER BY`, `SKIP`, `LIMIT` |
| Patterns | `(n:<type>)`, `-[:<relation>]->`, `<-[...]-`, `-[...]-`, `[:<relation>\|<relation>]`, `*1..3`, `{<attr>: <value>}` |
| Expressions | `AND OR XOR NOT`, `= <> < <= > >=`, `IN`, `STARTS WITH`, `ENDS WITH`, `CONTAINS`, `IS NULL`, `n:<type>`, `(n)-[:<relation>]->()`, `CASE`, `+ - * / %` |
| Functions | `count(*)`, `count(DISTINCT ...)`, `collect`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `avg`, `labels`, `type`, `keys`, `properties`, `coalesce`, `size`, `head`, `last`, `toString`, `toInteger`, `toFloat`, `toLower`, `toUpper`, `trim`, `substring`, `split`, `replace`, `abs`, `ceil`, `floor`, `round` |

A variable-length relationship (`*1..3`) needs an upper bound of at most 5.
Anything else (`CREATE` and other writes, `CALL`, `UNION`, named paths,
unbounded `*`, `id()`) is `query.unsupported`; `error.details` names the
construct and an alternative. Decimal numbers come back as strings.

Examples:

- `graph query 'MATCH (a:<type>)-[:<relation>]->(b)-[:<relation>]->(c) RETURN a, c.<attr>' --json`
- `graph query 'MATCH (n:<type>) WHERE NOT (n)-[:<relation>]->() RETURN n' --json`
- `graph query 'MATCH (n:<type>)-[:<relation>]->(m) RETURN m.<attr>, count(n) AS total ORDER BY total DESC' --json`
- `graph query 'MATCH (n:<type>) WHERE n.id = $id RETURN n' --param id=<id> --json`
